name: Conditional Access Directive
impact_assessment: none (proposed before impact assessments were introduced)
summary: The Directive bans commercial dealing in devices that give unauthorised access to pay-TV and online subscription services. The Commission's second report (2008) found that piracy adapted to new technology and that the hoped-for growth of cross-border pay services had largely not happened. No later evaluation or empirical study was found.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: European Commission (2008), Second report on the implementation of Directive 98/84/EC on the legal protection of services based on, or consisting of, conditional access, COM(2008) 593 (with SEC(2008) 2506)
literature.title: Second report on the implementation of Directive 98/84/EC on the legal protection of services based on, or consisting of, conditional access
literature.headline: Piracy adapts well to technological progress; little cross-border growth of conditional-access services, though some pay-TV services are offered across borders
literature.summary_plain: Ten years on, the Commission found the ban on pirate decoders in place but piracy still adapting, and little cross-border pay-TV market.
